newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rabobank/Robeco deal could face legal hurdle - VEB.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank/Robeco deal could face legal hurdle - VEB.

text.p: A Dutch shareholder's lobby group is considering legal action to stop co-operative bank Rabobank's 1.3 billion guilder purchase of control of the giant Robeco funds management group in its current form.

The Dutch Association of Shareholders (VEB) said the deal should not proceed unless more information was provided and the deal was put to shareholders in the Robeco funds, demands which have been rejected by Robeco.
Rabobank, the Netherlands' third largest bank, is paying 500 million guilders for 50 percent of Robecam, the Robeco group's management company, in a deal to be finalised next month.
Under terms announced in June, Rabobank would pay another 500 million guilders to move after four years to full ownership of Robecam.
Shareholders in Rabocam would also receive 100 million guilders in cash and annual dividends of 45 million guilders for four years.
Robecam is owned 40 percent by 16 Robeco group funds and 60 percent by staff, but the funds receive most of the profits.
VEB director Peter-Paul de Vries said individual shareholders in the funds should be given a chance to vote on the deal as their funds would no longer share in Robecam's profits.
He said they should also receive more information on the takeover, including the future level of management fees.
De Vries said Rabobank may try to lift Rabocam's profits by increasing the funds' management fees, which are below the industry average, and cutting research and development spending.
He said the VEB, which has some 15,000 private and institutional members, was considering legal action. "Of course we are looking at it," he said declining to elaborate.
Robeco spokesman Hans de Klerk said shareholders would not be given commercially confidential details on management fees and there was no legal obligation to seek their approval.
But he said that as Rabobank was a co-operative, profit maximisation was not the objective of the takeover.
"It's a growth objective that (they) have," he said.
Rabobank has set Robeco the goal of doubling its funds under management to 150 billion guilders within four years if it is to take up its option to move to 100 percent ownership.
A spokesman for the Dutch central bank declined to say if the bank was happy with the transaction its current form.
He said: "You can imagine we know the facts", but declined to elaborate.
